anomalies.observed: In the 'Capacitive Touch Button (TSC)' block on the root sheet, the two net labels NET0011 and NET0019 are attached to one and the same node. That single node fans out to the 22 nF capacitor C8 (other side to GND) and to the left terminal of the 1 kΩ series resistor R14, whose right terminal goes to the A3 'BTN' electrode pin. In other words the electrode-drive line and the sampling-capacitor line are shorted together, and the sampling capacitor sits on the electrode net.
anomalies.expected: The STM32 Touch Sensing Controller needs the sampling capacitor on its own dedicated group IO and the sense electrode on a separate group IO (per the specification: one pin drives the pad through the 1 kΩ series resistor, while the 22 nF sampling capacitor connects from a different TSC pin to GND). The two nets NET0011 and NET0019 must therefore stay separate.

evidence.quote: Capacitive Touch Button (TSC) block, root sheet /PCB.kicad_sch: labels 'NET0011' and 'NET0019' joined on the same wire that feeds R14 (1k) and C8 (22n) to the A3 'BTN' electrode (pin 1); A3 'SHLD' (pin 2) to GND.
TSC_G2_IO2: U2 pin 57 (PB5) — R8 (1 kΩ series resistor) — A2 pin "BTN" (the touch electrode) ... TSC_G2_IO4: U2 pin 59 (PB7) — C14 (22 nF to GND) — this is the TSC sampling capacitor for the group

anomalies.impact: The MCU's electrode-drive pin and sampling-capacitor pin are shorted and the sampling capacitor is placed on the electrode line, so the charge-transfer measurement the TSC peripheral relies on cannot work; the capacitive touch button will not sense touches.

parsed.summary: The schematic largely matches the specification, but in the capacitive-touch block the two TSC nets NET0011 and NET0019 are drawn on a single node together with the 22 nF sampling capacitor C8 and the 1 kΩ electrode resistor R14, shorting the electrode pin to the sampling-capacitor pin and defeating the touch-sensing circuit.
